item.title: Czech SMR environmental impact assessment submitted
item.description: ČEZ has submitted the Environmental Impact Assessment documentation to the Ministry of the Environment for its Rolls-Royce SMR small modular reactor project in Temelín.
item.wnn:fullText:
The submission of the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is a key part of the permitting process and assesses the potential impact on the area from the proposed small modular reactor (SMR) project, as well as putting forward steps to minimise any impact.

ČEZ said: "We pay significant attention to water. Water availability is one of the basic criteria when selecting and preparing locations for SMRs. Preparation includes detailed surveys and long-term monitoring focused, among other things, on water resources and their future availability. The results so far confirm that water availability does not represent an obstacle, even when taking into account the worsening drought."

The ministry will assess the documentation and take public comments. The EIA process is expected to be completed by the end of 2027.

Daniel Beneš, Chairman and CEO of ČEZ, said: "We are counting on small modular reactors alongside large nuclear power plants and renewable sources. They are also a great opportunity for Czech companies. The supply chain for small modular reactors is being formed right now. Companies that join this global chain at the very beginning have the potential to win orders for decades to come, because they will supply the entire SMR fleet in the Czech Republic and abroad."

Background

The Rolls-Royce SMR is a 470 MWe design based on a small pressurised water reactor. It will provide consistent baseload generation for at least 60 years. Ninety percent of the SMR - measuring about 16 metres by 4 metres - will be built in factory conditions, limiting activity on-site primarily to assembly of pre-fabricated, pre-tested, modules which significantly reduces project risk and has the potential to drastically shorten build schedules.

In October 2024, Rolls-Royce SMR was selected by ČEZ to deploy up to 3 GW of electricity in the Czech Republic, and ČEZ took a 20% stake in Rolls-Royce SMR. The plan is for this first SMR to be deployed in the area of the Temelín site (which already has two gigawatt-scale VVER-1000 units), with further projects being developed for coal-fired power plant sites, including Tušimice.

In June 2025, Rolls-Royce SMR was selected as the UK government's preferred technology for the country's first SMR project. In November, the UK government announced that Wylfa on the island of Anglesey, North Wales, would be the site to host the three Rolls-Royce SMR units. It said the site - where a Magnox plant is being decommissioned - could potentially host up to eight SMRs. A final investment decision is expected to be taken in 2029.

The submission of the EIA follows the signing of Early Works Contracts between Rolls-Royce SMR and ČEZ, supporting the preparation of the site and working to secure the permits required for construction at Temelín. It also builds on a memorandum of understanding signed earlier this year between Rolls-Royce SMR, ČEZ and the Czech Ministry of Industry and Trade which enabled site preparation activities for further deployments in Tušimice and Dětmarovice.

The UK project is expected to be the first Rolls-Royce SMR deployed, with Temelín to host the second, with a target operational date "in the second half of the 2030s".

item.title: Agreement signed on second Polish nuclear power plant
item.description: Poland's Ministry of Energy, Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe and Polska Grupa Energetyczna have signed an agreement defining the division of tasks and principles of cooperation in preparing the construction of the country's second nuclear power plant.
item.wnn:fullText:
In September 2021, it was announced that six large pressurised water reactors with a combined installed capacity of 6-9 GWe could be built by 2040 as part of the country's plan to reduce its reliance on coal. According to the adopted schedule, the construction of the first nuclear power plant would start in 2026, with the first reactor - with a capacity of 1.0-1.6 GWe - being commissioned in 2033. Subsequent units would be implemented every 2 to 3 years.

The Lubiatowo-Kopalino site in the Choczewo municipality in Pomerania in northern Poland was selected as the preferred location for the country's first large nuclear power plant, which will have a capacity of 3,750 MWe, using Westinghouse's AP1000 technology. An agreement setting a plan for the delivery of the plant was signed in May 2023 by Westinghouse, Bechtel and Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe (PEJ). Construction is scheduled to begin in 2028.

Work has now started on the second nuclear power plant, with Bełchatów and Konin the preferred locations.

PEJ - a special-purpose vehicle 100% owned by Poland's State Treasury - is to be the investor and coordinator of the second nuclear power plant project, while state-owned power company Polska Grupa Energetyczna (PGE) will prepare site analyses and preliminary feasibility studies in collaboration with potential technology suppliers, according to a new agreement signed by the Ministry of Energy, PEJ and PGE. The document introduces the assumptions of the updated Polish nuclear power programme, adopted by the Council of Ministers on 29 September.

"The cooperation is intended to ensure the effective use of the resources and experience of both companies and to improve investment preparation, also through appropriate coordination of activities at the government administration level," the Ministry of Energy said. It noted that PEJ was responsible for preparing the design of the first Polish nuclear power plant, while PGE - whose group includes PGE Energia Jądrowa - also has experience in preparing nuclear projects.

Under the recent update to the country's nuclear power programme, the first unit is now scheduled to start commercial operation in 2036, and the plant is expected to reach full capacity by 2038 - three years later than previously planned.

The ministry said a competitive dialogue was under way to select a technology supplier and project contractor for the second plant. The USA, France, and Canada have joined the process. "A key element of this process will be for suppliers to prepare preliminary feasibility studies for power plants using the technologies they offer," it said. "The aim of the procedure is to select a comprehensive offer encompassing technology, investment financing, and elements of broader strategic cooperation. For the second power plant, as for the first, the proven technology of large-scale Generation III+ light-water reactors is being considered."

Key milestones for the second power plant under the updated nuclear power programme are: the selection of a strategic partner and technology in 2027; construction to start around 2032; and the first unit to start up around 2040 – one year behind the previous schedule.

The ministry said the final decision on the second plant would be made after conducting the necessary research and analyses to confirm the feasibility of the investment.

Agreement welcomed

"The construction of a second nuclear power plant is an undertaking that requires close cooperation between the state and state-owned companies," said Minister of State Assets Wojciech Balczun. "Today's agreement demonstrates our exemplary cooperation, effectively combining the expertise and experience of various entities to achieve the common goal of Poland's energy security."

Wojciech Wrochna, Deputy Minister of Energy and Government Plenipotentiary for Strategic Energy Infrastructure, added: "We now have site analyses, feasibility studies, and technology selection ahead of us. We intend to conduct this process competitively to develop favourable investment implementation conditions, taking into account not only technology but also financing and long-term strategic cooperation."

"We are embarking on the second nuclear power plant with something we didn't have at the start of the first investment: experience from the first project," said Marek Woszczyk, President of the Management Board of PEJ. "We know how to manage administrative processes, organise dialogue with partners, and prepare for implementation of a project of this scale."

Dariusz Lubera, President of the Management Board of PGE, said: "I believe that the combination of knowledge, experience, and competence of both companies will enable the successful implementation of this ambitious project, which is of strategic importance for the future of the Polish energy sector and the entire economy."
